$comment: The source lock of this packet: what was checked against upstream, how, and when. Revisions are named as in target.json. 'files' gives the git blob id (git hash-object) of each source file the selected method depends on, at each revision, so a later reader can check a checkout, a release or a sources JAR against it. 'correspondence' records which published artifacts carry the same sources. Checked by hand by the positive stream; a note, not evidence of a build or a replay.
how: git init --bare; git fetch --depth=2 --filter=blob:none https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-security SHA; parents read from the fetched commit object; tags fetched as refs/tags/T and resolved with git rev-parse T^{commit}

dependencies.$comment: BCrypt needs only the JDK (java.nio.charset, java.security.MessageDigest, java.security.SecureRandom, java.util.Arrays). The crypto module's optional dependencies, spring-jcl 5.2.0.RC1 (gradle/dependency-management.gradle) and bcpkix-jdk15on, are not used by BCrypt.
dependencies.build: Gradle 5.5.1 wrapper (services.gradle.org); buildscript: io.spring.gradle:spring-build-conventions:0.0.23.RELEASE and spring-boot-gradle-plugin 2.2.0.M3 from repo.spring.io/plugins-snapshot and plugins.gradle.org; ext.springVersion 5.2.0.RC1, springDataVersion Moore-RC2, reactorVersion Dysprosium-M3; no SNAPSHOT dependency pinned.

correspondence.finding: BCrypt.java identical to before's; a milestone, published only to repo.spring.io.

Differs from after's by the removed unused import java.io.UnsupportedEncodingException and `private final void encipher` becoming `private void encipher` (an access flag on a callee of hashpw(byte[],String)); hashpw(String,String) itself is the same source.
Not before's code: BCrypt was rewritten on master before 5.2.0 (hundreds of lines differ).
